result.title: FoveaDet: Software-Hardware Co-Design of Foveated CNN-Transformer for Object Detection
result.comment: 5 pages, 6 figures. Submitted to IEEE ISCAS 2027
result.summary: Deploying real-time object detection on power-constrained edge platforms is challenging as processing full-resolution frames is often computationally redundant. Inspired by biological foveation which assigns variable resolution based on visual saliency, we propose a novel software-hardware co-design framework called FoveaDet. On the software side, FoveaDet dynamically identifies salient regions to predict fixation points, followed by aggressive patch pruning in Vision Transformers (ViT) to discard irrelevant background data. To mitigate slowdowns from sequential patch generation, we implement optimized interpolation and patch selection algorithms. Evaluated on standard GPUs, this foveated approach reduces floating-point operations by 65.4% to 92.2% and accelerates inference by 4.76x, while suffering a negligible mAP drop compared to dense baselines. To eliminate hardware bottlenecks, we complement the algorithm with a custom RISC-V core featuring specialized instructions to accelerate the foveated processing pipeline. FoveaDet provides a scalable, efficient architecture capable of unlocking advanced vision processing on severely constrained mobile platforms.

AI.brief_summary: FoveaDet 提出受生物中央凹启发的软硬件协同设计：先动态预测显著区域与注视点，再据此在 ViT 中激进裁剪冗余 patch，并配套带专用指令的 RISC-V 核；在 GPU 上减少 65.4%–92.2% FLOPs、提速 4.76 倍且 mAP 下降可忽略。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「注视点预测 + 显著区域 patch 裁剪」涉及「看哪里」的证据筛选与计算分配，可能与 LVR 中视觉证据获取成本、动态计算预算的权衡相关，可供核查；但工作面向边缘检测部署，未涉及推理状态或 latent 生成，联系较为间接。
